newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, U.S. to discuss phytosanitary issues.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, U.S. to discuss phytosanitary issues.

text.p: Brazilian and U.S. officials will discuss phytosanitary conditions for products such as fresh fruit and U.S. wheat at a meeting on July 30-31 in Brasilia, a Brazilian Agriculture Ministry official said.

U.S. wheat exports to Brazil have effectively come to a halt since September last year following the expiry of a waiver which had been in place since the introduction of new Brazilian entry requirements in January 1996.
The problem centers around the tilletia controversa kuhn or TCK fungus which has been found in very limited areas in northern U.S. states.
In theory wheat from five states in the U.S. can still be exported to Brazil even under the new regulations but the U.S. system cannot guarantee the origin of wheat, the official said.
Brazil's Wheat Industries Association (Abitrigo) has recently asked the government to consider ways to facilitate U.S. imports given weather-induced disruptions in supply from Argentina.
But no decision will be taken until after the meeting at the end of this month, the official said.
"We have to wait and see what new proposals the U.S. delegation brings and then we will talk. There will be no decision until then," he said.
